A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable versions of the same BTimer work, and all supplied pages were inspected. v2 includes supplementary Sections A–D; v3 ends at the references. This is an identifiable omission from the supplied PDF, not an extraction failure; it does not establish that the underlying experiments were withdrawn.

before.justification: v2 reports original dynamic and static reconstruction results, qualitative demonstrations, and supplementary quantitative ablations and training analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains original DyCheck, NVIDIA Dynamic Scene, RE10K, and Tanks & Temples results, alongside DAVIS demonstrations and qualitative ablations.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same transformer architecture, timestamp embeddings, pixel-aligned Gaussian prediction, RGB loss, NTE module, inference procedure, and three-stage training curriculum. The new discussion of temporal deformation is a limitation, not a method revision.

E1.justification: The training datasets and main evaluation benchmarks remain unchanged. v2's supplementary coverage of SORA scenes and static demonstrations spanning drone and 360-degree views is no longer documented in v3; these are limited omissions from the reported scenario coverage.

E2.justification: The NVIDIA quantitative table drops NSFF and MonoNeRF, although both remain in the quality-speed plot and MonoNeRF remains in qualitative comparisons. Omitting the supplement also removes the RE10K comparisons with PixelNeRF, AttnRend, and MuRF, plus the training-cost comparison involving LVSM and LRM. Several distinct comparison groups are therefore reduced or absent.

E3.justification: v3 no longer reports the supplementary two-view static-model RE10K configuration or the controlled training comparison using 1, 8, and 32 GPUs. The retained main-text training budgets and benchmark protocols are unchanged; the PDFs do not establish rerunning those experiments under revised settings.

E4.justification: The qualitative component ablations remain, but v3 omits Table S4's quantitative tests of pretraining, static co-training, and interpolation supervision. Figures S3–S4 and their accompanying compute-scaling and batch-size analyses also disappear, substantially reducing supporting analysis.

E5.justification: Neither supplied PDF reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty bands. v2's supplementary training curves do not report such uncertainty either.

E6.justification: Retained scores are unchanged, including BTimer's DyCheck PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS of 16.52/0.570/0.338 and NVIDIA PSNR/LPIPS of 25.82/0.086. However, v3 omits substantial result entries: two NVIDIA table rows, supplementary static PSNR/SSIM comparisons, the two-view static result, and the four-context NVIDIA ablation scores in Table S4. This changes reported evidence without showing a same-setting performance gain.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation, timestamp definitions, Gaussian parameterization, unprojection equation, and loss remain equivalent. Neither version contains additional theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: Both versions retain the claims of motion-aware feed-forward bullet-time reconstruction, generalization through static/dynamic training, NTE support for fast motion, and efficient competitive reconstruction. The abstract, introduction, and conclusion do not materially redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: v3 newly explains that correspondences are implicit, the representation cannot express temporal deformations, and recovering explicit geometric motion requires post-processing. It removes v2's explicit view-extrapolation limitation and proposed generative-prior remedy. The supplementary interpretation of amortized computation and large-batch training is also absent.

D1.justification: Omitting Sections A–B and Tables S1/S5 removes dataset sampling multipliers, scale factors, detailed counts, the Kubric-MV rendering recipe, approximately four-day training cost, and exact inference-memory measurements. v3 also removes the code/checkpoint-release promises while retaining the project link; actual resource availability cannot be inferred.

R1.justification: Section 2 shortens the deformation-parameterization discussion and removes the discussion of optimization-assisted initialization and guidance. Eight references disappear, including G3R, Gaussian-Flow, Dynamic 3D Gaussians, and Depth Anything V2; VBench is added to the bibliography. The central research positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: Most main-text prose and the five-section narrative remain substantially intact. v3 shortens related work, compresses the ablations into numbered prose, reorders the conclusion and limitations, adds Broader Impact, and omits the supplementary section block. Several former figure references incorrectly become references to Section 4.2.1.

P2.justification: v3 adopts a single-column layout, removes the opening teaser, merges dynamic Tables 1–2 into Table 1, and presents static Table 3 as Figure 7. It combines v2 Figures 7–8 into Figure 6 and Figures 9–10 into Figure 8, rearranging retained panels. All supplementary figures and tables are absent.

improvement.justification: The supplied v3 adds a useful explicit-motion limitation, but loses v2's entire supplement, including essential dataset preparation details, additional quantitative comparisons, and numerical ablation and training analyses. Main claims and retained scores remain unchanged while references to the missing supplement persist and several figure pointers become incorrect. These omissions substantially weaken reproducibility and the evidence available to assess the paper.
